answer: Peer-prediction scoring pays for knowing what peers do not: each epoch asks which marble lantern survives a forge and each answer carries a forecast of the pool vote. Credit is the real popularity of your pick minus the popularity you predicted, so only right, surprisingly common answers pay. A thousand wallets from one farmer answer alike and forecast each other perfectly: their surprise term is zero, so the cluster earns nothing however many keys it mints. Honest weight thus needs a contrarian view that proves right. Extra identities need fresh insight per epoch, which cannot be minted.
